question.problem:
Evaluate the series
${\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{2}{(n+3)(n+4)}.$
Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{1}{(n+3)(n+4)}=\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+4}.$*

${\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{2}{(n+3)(n+4)}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the series can be written as

$$
2{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(n+3)(n+4)}
$$

We are also given that

$$
\frac{1}{(n+3)(n+4)}=\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+4}.
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
2{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n+3}-\frac{1}{n+4}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{3} & =2[(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{4} & =2[(\frac{1}{6}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{8})] \\ {s}_{5} & =2[(\frac{1}{6}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{8}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{8}}-\frac{1}{9})] \\ {s}_{6} & =2[(\frac{1}{6}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{8}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{8}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{9}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{9}}-\frac{1}{10})]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms except for the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{N} & =2(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{N+4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{2}{(n+3)(n+4)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }2(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{N+4}) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
